recipes.name: Poblano Chile Enchiladas
ingredients_raw: 2 (8 ounce) skinless, boneless chicken breast halves

steps.text: Combine water, chicken, onion, garlic, and bouillon in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer until chicken is no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, about 40 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Transfer chicken to a plate to cool. Reserve 1 cup broth and discard the rest.

Roast poblano chiles over an open flame (or underneath a broiler) until the skin has blackened on all sides. Place chiles into a plastic bag (or bowl covered with plastic wrap), and let cool, about 30 minutes. Peel blackened skin off cooled peppers, and remove seeds and membranes.
Transfer poblano flesh to a blender; add 1 cup reserved chicken broth and sour cream. Purée until smooth.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry tortillas, one at a time, until softened and beginning to crisp, 10 to 15 seconds. Stack fried tortillas on a plate.
Pour puréed poblano mixture into the skillet and simmer for 10 minutes.
While the sauce is cooking, slice cooled chicken into 1/4-inch strips.

Using tongs, dip one tortilla into hot sauce in the skillet, coating both sides, then place onto a work surface. Arrange some chicken in the center, then tightly roll tortilla around filling. Place enchilada, seam-side down, into a serving dish. Repeat to make remaining enchiladas.
Spoon remaining sauce over enchiladas, then sprinkle with mozzarella.

raw_recipe.headline: Poblano Chile Enchiladas
raw_recipe.description: These poblano enchiladas feature pan-fried corn tortillas filled with chicken, dipped in a creamy roasted poblano sauce, and topped with mozzarella cheese.

review.reviewBody: This was great. I made a few changes. I didn't fry in the tortillas in oil. I placed the chicken and some cheese in the tortillas, rolled them up and placed them in a baking dish, topped with the sauce and cheese. I placed them under the broiler until the cheese was golden-brown. Yum!

I am really glad I saw this recipe, as doing Poblano peppers was a first for me. I read many reviews to get an idea of the savoriness, plus other people's likes and dislikes. I gleaned favorite additions of some, mixed with my tastes, and I thought it came out pretty great. I made two dishes of it, and gave one to some family, everyone liked it. To address the issue of the sauce being "too thin", I first sauteed the onion & garlic (heavier on the garlic than what was called for), then added it to my blender, with the reduced broth that came from my roasted chicken, the juices from the onion/garlic mixed with added chicken broth, plus the roasted peppers and pureed it. I poured it into the saucepan, adding roasted garlic, jalapeno slices, 2 cans of green chilies, and slowly added the sour cream, (I didn't use all the original recipe called for). As for spices, I used salt, little bl pepper, smoked paprika, a dash of celery seed, cumin & garlic granules. I added chicken broth along the way, as needed. Enter shredded chicken (I set to the side of the pan, so I could dip my crisped Sprouted grain corn tortillas into it prior to filling). Just about everything I used was organic, minus the peppers. I filled each enchilada with mix, pepper jack cheese, and extra sauce. Covered with a Mexican cheese blend(which I would change to something more flavorful next time), and baked in wither a 375' or 400' oven for about 12 minutes. Yum! Other change next time...I would add more poblanos.

made this 3xs, twice with chicken, once with pork. Everyone loved it. My changes: 1. roasted the meat (season the meat before roasting) instead if boiling. 2. Instead of chicken broth, I used the broth from the bottom of pan (from roasting) 3. For a more depth of flavor, I Sautéed 1 onion, small handful of corn, 3 cloves garlic, and 2 tomatoes w salt pepper and pinch of cumin. 4. When assembly: dip the tortilla (yes I fried mine) into the poblano sauce, sprinkle Mexican blend cheese, add some meat, add small spoon of the sautéed veggies. Fold and place in a greased baking dish. Thank put more cheese on top and bake till bubbly and almost golden brown. I serve with fresh cilantro and lime wedge. Hubby said he would pay $14 for a plate of this at a restaurant. So yummy! Yes it takes a lot of time but sooo worth it. Also side note: depending where your poblanos a are from, sometimes they are hotter than normal. Make sure you taste your poblano sauce - if the heat is not hot enough dice jalepenos and ad to the sauce. (I had to do that once)

I am eating the leftovers from last nite while I am writing this and they are even better the next day! I must say I couldn't find poblanos so I used a can of green chilis instead. I also used 4 chicken hindquarters that I did in the crock-pot and used the broth they made. I also used Monteray Jack cheese and assembled them like a lasagna instead of rolling them. They were ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS!!!! I can't wait to try them with the poblanos! I will take these OVER and Over! Thanks Olga!

These were really good. One of the best enchiladas I've eaten. However, I did make some significant changes that I think really helped. 1st, instead of tossing out the remaining broth, I skimmed out the onions and set aside, later adding a spoonful to the chicken filling inside the enchilada when wrapping. I also enhanced the filling by a generous sprinkling of mazarella cheese, so the filling was moister and a little creamy from the cheese. The other change was the last step not mentioned in this recipe..., I covered the enchiladas with foil and put into a preheated 350 degree oven for 10 minutes. Then, them out of the oven, and topped the enchiladas with shredded sharp cheddar cheese, then covered back with foil for 10 more minutes. The final touch was to remove the foil and continue baking until the cheese on top just started to turn brown. So Good!!!

This was delicious. I followed some of the advice in some of the reviews and made the following changes: used 3 cups of chicken broth instead of water and bouillon (because I just don't keep boullion on hand), added about 1/2 tsp of cumin, 1/2 tsp white pepper, was pretty generous with the salt and some chopped cilantro to the blender of sauce. After assembled I threw it in the oven under a broiler for a few minutes because I like my cheese browned and a bit crispy on enchiladas. Great flavor without being too spicy so it was good even for the little ones.

This was excellent - texture, flavor, everything tasted like authentic perfect enchiladas. I did brown the tortillas up a bit before rolling them and added corn, zucchini, and red bell peppers to the enchiladas that I separately sautéed. Also browned the chicken a bit first as other people have recommended. Although the poblano sauce was amazing, it did lack a little spice (could have been due to weak poblanos) so I plan to add a jalapeño to the mix next time. Overall thought I’m thrilled to have found a wonderful enchilada recipe!

Excellent!! I made a cheese enchilada version of this recipe with a few other adjustments. I roasted the poblanos as directed, then pureed them in a blender with plain greek yogurt (substituted for sour cream)and low sodium organic chicken broth. I put the poblano sauce in a skillet to simmer on LOW for ten minutes, stirring in 1 tsp sea salt, 1/2 tsp garlic powder and 1/4 tsp cumin. I sauteed chopped purple onion with 2 cloves of minced garlic on medium heat until the onions were soft, then set these aside. If you want to add heat to this recipe, I think you could add two seeded and chopped jalapenos to the saute. 


For the filling, I combined 2 cups white cheddar with 2 cups sharp orange cheddar. I prepared white corn tortillas as directed, very lightly frying them corn oil. I dipped the a tortilla liberally in the poblano sauce, then filled with a small amount of the onion/garlic sautee and a liberal amount of cheese. Roll and place the seam down in glass pan. Pour remaining poblano sauce over the top of enchiladas, and liberally sprinkle with cheese. Top with one to two tablespoons of chopped cilantro. Bake at 375 for 15 to 20 minutes until cheese is melted. I wouldn't try to brown these as I don't want to scorch the yogurt-based poblano sauce.

I made this today for Hubby. He loved it. Not sure why the recipe would say discard the rest of the cooking broth. It seemed like such a waste. While my Chicken was cooling and Chilies were roasting I cooked down the broth to concentrate the flavors. I also used Jack cheese instead of Mozzarella. Cilantro and green onion for garnish..Yummy. Next time I'll add a couple of Roasted Jalapeno's with the Poblanos.

Delicious! I used freshly roasted poblanos from my local farmers market. I used my slow cooker to cook the chicken with broth, onions, garlic and cumin. I also used flour tortillas since that's what I had on hand. I added the onions from slow cooker to enchiladas. I also subbed white cheddar for the mozzarella. Lots of flavor and easy recipe!

I have made these twice now and they are absolutely fantastic! There are a lot of steps and it takes much longer to make than listed, but totally worth it! We travel to Mexico often and eat Mexican food a minimum of three times per week. I used the chicken breast of a Costco rotisserie chicken to cut time. They are tender and juicy. I used low sodium chicken broth instead of the bullion, chopped up the chicken first and simmered for 10 minutes for the flavor. I don't think the sauce needs to be simmered for 10 minutes after blending it because I put them in the oven for 25 minutes to heat through and melt the cheese like you would with most other enchiladas anyway.
This is a great recipe. The sauce is particularly good. I used the recipe as is except added cumin to the sauce and garnished with fresh cilantro.

Heated my tortillas over my gas stove flame. Used rotisserie chicken, substituted Greek yogurt for sour cream, added cumin, Sazón Complete seasoning, 2 cilantro bouillon cubes, cayenne pepper and lime juice to my sauce. Covered the enchiladas with Chahuahua cheese...Great use of garden-fesh poblano peppers. Wonderful!!!
One of my favorite mexi dishes to make!
So tasty! I did what other reviewers did and skipped the steps to warm tortilla and dip in sauce - I just rolled the burritos, covered in sauce and baked in the oven.
We've been using this recipe for years now. The entire family loves it every time!

These turned out SO GOOD! LOVE the poblano sauce! I followed the recipe except I did pop them in the oven for a little bit. I’m making again tonight but trying a quicker way with rotisserie chicken and layering the tortillas, chicken, sauce and cheese. I’m sure it will be just as great since it’s the sauce that is the main thing, in my opinion. Thank you for such a yummy recipe!

Instead of water/bullion I just used chicken broth. Also, next time I will make with flour tortillas instead of corn.finally next time I will just use a rotisserie chicken instead of boiling. I added a few dashes of cumin to the poblano mixture. Good flavor for the sauce.will make again
